title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SPECIAL CIVIL ACT ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AGREEMENT UNDER ARTICLE 4 OF THE MUTUAL DEFENSE TREATY BETWEEN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA AND THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, REGARDING FACILITIES AND AREAS AND THE STATUS OF UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE SPECIAL CIVIL ACT ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE AGREEMENT UNDER ARTICLE 4 OF THE MUTUAL DEFENSE TREATY BETWEEN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA AND THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, REGARDING FACILITIES AND AREAS AND THE STATUS OF UNITED STATES ARMED FORCES IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters necessary for enforcement of the Special Civil Act on the Implementation of the Agreement under Article 4 of the Mutual Defense Treaty between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America, regarding Facilities and Areas and the Status of United States Armed Forces in the Republic of Korea (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") and Article 23 of the Agreement under Article 4 of the Mutual Defense Treaty between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America, regarding Facilities and Areas and the Status of United States Armed Forces in the Republic of Korea (hereinafter referred to as the "Agreement").

Article 2 (Applications for Compensation for Damage)
(1) A victim who has suffered damage from an incident to be handled under Article 23 (5) through (7) of the Agreement, or a surviving family member of such victim, who intends to apply for compensation for damage shall submit an application for compensation for damage to the district council affiliated with the Headquarters Council under Article 10 of the State Compensation Act having jurisdiction over the applicant's address or the place where the incident occurred (hereinafter referred to as the "Council"). <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>
(2) Upon receiving an application under paragraph (1), the chairperson of the Council shall report or notify its receipt to the Minister of Justice and the United States military authorities (hereinafter referred to as the "United States military authorities"). <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>

Article 3 (Investigation of Incidents)
(1) The chairperson of the Council who receives an application under Article 2 (1), or a person acting under the chairperson's order, shall examine the necessary evidence within one month and refer the matter to the Council. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>
(2) Where necessary to investigate an application, the chairperson of the Council shall request cooperation from the United States authorities without delay.
(3) The chairperson of the Council may conduct necessary investigations into incidents falling under Article 23 (5) through (7) of the Agreement that occur within the Council's jurisdiction even before an application under Article 2 (1) is filed. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>

Article 4 (Deliberation and Decisions, etc.)
(1) On the basis of an investigation under Article 3, the Council shall make a compensation decision in accordance with the State Compensation Act and its Enforcement Decree for cases under Article 23 (5) and (7) of the Agreement. For cases under Article 23 (6) of the Agreement, the Council shall deliberate and report the results to the Minister of Justice without delay, attaching the deliberation records.
(2) Upon receiving the report and records under paragraph (1), the Minister of Justice shall assess compensation under Article 23 (6) of the Agreement.

Article 5 (Notification of Decisions, etc.)
(1) Where the Council decides under Article 4 to pay compensation or dismiss the application, it shall notify the applicant of the outcome in writing. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>
(2) Where the Minister of Justice assesses compensation, the Minister shall notify the applicant and the relevant Council; upon receiving that notification, the Council shall send the report under Article 23 (6) (a) of the Agreement to the United States military authorities without delay.

Article 6 (Payment of Compensation)
(1) Where an applicant who has been notified of a decision to pay compensation intends to receive payment, the applicant shall apply for payment without delay, attaching written consent to the relevant Council's decision on payment.
(2) Upon receiving an application for payment under paragraph (1), the chairperson of the Council shall take the necessary steps for payment of compensation without delay. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>

Article 7 (Reports of Payment and Requests for Reimbursement)
(1) The chairperson of a Council or the head of an administrative office who has made a payment under Article 23 (5) (b) of the Agreement pursuant to a court judgment and Article 6 shall report or notify that fact to the Minister of Justice without delay, attaching a receipt. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>
(2) Upon receiving a report or notification of payment under paragraph (1), the Minister of Justice shall take necessary measures concerning notification of payment and requests for reimbursement to the United States military authorities under Article 23 (5) (d) and (e) of the Agreement. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>

Article 8 (Assistance with Claims, etc.)
(1) A person who has suffered maritime damage referred to in Article 23 (5) (g) of the Agreement to which paragraph (5) of that Article does not apply, or who has suffered or is likely to suffer damage under Article 23 (10) of the Agreement, may apply to the Minister of Justice for assistance with a claim or other necessary measures.
(2) An application under paragraph (1) shall state its purport and grounds and shall be accompanied by the necessary evidence. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>
(3) Where the Minister of Justice considers an application under paragraph (1) well-founded, the Minister shall provide the necessary assistance.
(4) Where the Minister of Justice decides not to provide assistance or has completed providing assistance, the Minister shall notify the applicant of the result.

Article 9 (Assistance with Litigation)
(1) A victim under Article 8 (1) who has instituted litigation may apply to the Minister of Justice for the following assistance with the litigation: <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>
1. Collection of necessary evidence;
2. Introduction or referral to an attorney-at-law;
3. Advice concerning litigation;
4. Assistance concerning use of necessary foreign currency;
5. Other matters necessary for litigation.
(2) Article 8 shall apply mutatis mutandis to assistance with litigation. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>

Article 10 (Damage to Government Property)
(1) Where property under the jurisdiction of the head of an administrative office (including the Minister of National Court Administration and the Secretary General of the National Assembly) suffers damage referred to in Article 23 of the Agreement, the head shall investigate the cause and extent of the damage and notify the Minister of Justice without delay.
(2) Upon receiving notification under paragraph (1), the Minister of Justice shall, following deliberation, assess the amount of damage and take necessary measures for reimbursement of that damage. <Amended on Feb. 4, 1980>

Article 10-2 (Processing of Personally Identifiable Information)
The Minister of Justice may process materials containing resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act where unavoidable to perform duties of assisting with claims for compensation for damage or supporting litigation under Article 5 of the Act.

Article 11 (Enforcement Rules)
Forms and other matters necessary for enforcement of this Decree shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Justice.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 4635, Feb. 16, 1970>

This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 9752, Feb. 4, 1980>

This Decree shall apply from February 1, 1980; provided, applications for payment of compensation received by the Headquarters Council or an affiliated district council as at the time this Decree enters into force shall be governed by the former practice.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 27960, Mar. 27, 2017>
(Decree Partially Amending the Enforcement Decree of the Certified Tax Accountant Act and Other Statutes and Regulations to Restrict Processing of Resident Registration Numbers, etc.)

This Decree shall enter into force on March 30, 2017. <Proviso omitted.>
